title: The Wrong Officer Signed the Extension: ITAT Delhi Voids a Rs. 208 Crore Assessment in Patanjali Ayurved
excerpt: A special audit under Section 142(2A) needs the Commissioner's approval. An extension of time to complete it does not — under the proviso to Section 142(2C) that power belongs to the Assessing Officer alone. When the Principal Commissioner granted the extension instead, the Delhi Tribunal held the assessment void ab initio, and the merits never came into play.

title: A Valuation Reference the AO Was Never Allowed to Make: Gujarat HC Quashes Reassessment Over the Pre-2012 Section 55A Rule
excerpt: The Gujarat High Court quashes a Section 148 reassessment built entirely on a DVO report the AO had no power to obtain. Under the pre-1 July 2012 Section 55A, a valuation reference was permissible only where the assessee's declared value was less than fair market value — not more — and the 2012 amendment cannot be applied backwards to save it.

title: Net Winnings, Not Gross: Hyderabad ITAT Deletes a Rs 3.54 Crore Online-Gaming Addition under Section 115BB
excerpt: A rummy player deposited Rs 3.84 crore in buy-ins to win Rs 3.54 crore back — a real cash loss. The Hyderabad ITAT holds that "winnings" under Section 115BB means net winnings and deletes the addition — but a coordinate Hyderabad bench has held the opposite, leaving the pre-AY 2024-25 gross-vs-net question genuinely open.

title: Commercial and Charitable Activities Can Co-Exist: Mumbai ITAT Restores Reliance Foundation Hospital's Registration
excerpt: The Mumbai ITAT holds that medical relief is an independent charitable purpose under Section 2(15), the commercial-activity proviso does not apply to it, and commercial scale is not commercial purpose — restoring the trust's Section 12AB registration and 80G approval.

title: Warranty Provision Is Not an Unascertained Liability: Gujarat HC Quashes Reassessment in Ammann India
excerpt: The Gujarat High Court quashes a Section 148A(d) reassessment order, holding that reopening based on ignorance of the Supreme Court's Rotork Controls ruling and material already on record amounts to nothing more than a change of opinion.

title: Secondment Salary Reimbursements Are Not Automatically FTS: ITAT Delhi in Honda R&D
excerpt: ITAT Delhi deleted a Rs. 21.53 crore FTS addition, holding that genuine cost-to-cost salary reimbursements for seconded employees depend on real employer facts.

title: Supreme Court Leaves Delhi HC's Pernod Ricard AMP Ruling Undisturbed
excerpt: The Revenue's SLP failed on a 384-day delay and on merits, leaving intact key findings on AMP expenditure, Section 14A, and seized-material additions.

title: ITAT Mumbai Deletes Cash Deposit Additions — Redeposits of Earlier Withdrawals Not "Unexplained"
excerpt: ITAT Mumbai rules that cash redeposits from earlier bank withdrawals cannot be treated as unexplained money u/s 69A. Full analysis of Nitinkumar Kacharia v. DCIT with key takeaways.

title: Transfer Pricing Adjustment ≠ Misreporting: Madras HC Quashes Section 270A Penalty on Verizon
excerpt: A landmark ruling draws a bright constitutional line — estimation-based TP adjustments cannot, in law, be equated with concealment or misrepresentation. The penalty regime has limits.

title: When the Revenue Cherry-Picks: ITAT Delhi on the Limited Risk Model, Berry Ratio, and the Boundaries of the "Other Method"
excerpt: A recent ITAT Delhi order doesn't just decide a case — it draws bright lines around four recurring transfer pricing and income tax controversies that affect every MNE operating in India.

title: Ancestral or Inherited Properties Can Be Attached Under PMLA: Delhi High Court
excerpt: The "it was my grandfather's house" defence is gone. A practitioner's analysis of Arun Suri v. Directorate of Enforcement and what it means for PMLA defence strategy.

title: Section 148 After the 2021 Amendment: What the Supreme Court Actually Held
excerpt: A practitioner's guide to the new reassessment regime — and where the battles are being fought today. Few provisions have produced as much litigation and confusion as Sections 147-151.

title: The New Income Tax Bill, 2025: What Changes, What Stays, and What It Means for You
excerpt: A practitioner's guide to India's biggest tax law overhaul in six decades — beyond the headlines. The Bill proposes to repeal and replace the Income Tax Act, 1961.
